subject: SLA negotiation: uptime & latency exception request (Acme Analytics)
messages:

To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2025-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SLA discussion — uptime & latency commitments

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the product demo last week — Acme is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before legal/procurement will sign, we need two things clarified in the SLA:

1) Uptime: Acme requires a 99.99% monthly uptime commitment for any production services that power our customer-facing features.
2) Credits: Automatic monthly service credits that scale with loss of uptime (we'd like a capped schedule with meaningful financial offsets).
3) Latency: We need a p99 latency target (not just p95) for API calls — our end users are sensitive to tail latency.

Attached is our exception request template and procurement timeline (we're targeting a PO by end of November). Can Redwood support an exception to your standard SLA or propose an alternative that aligns with Acme's risk profile?

Appreciate a proposal we can take to procurement.

—Tom

Hi Tom — thanks, and great to hear Acme liked the demo. Short answer: we can accommodate stronger commitments in certain deployment modes but there are trade-offs.

High level (what we typically offer):
- Hosted API: 99.9% monthly uptime SLA; credits up to 10% of monthly bill for sustained outages.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): higher SLOs available (commonly 99.95) with increased redundancy and an SLA amendment.
- Latency: our published targets focus on p95, but we can add p99 targets for Dedicated plans.

I'm attaching our latest SLA draft (Redwood-SLA-draft-v3.pdf) and can propose an exception pathway for Acme. If acceptable, I'd like to loop in Marcus (infra) and Rishi (sales lead) to align on operational commitments and credit mechanics.

Proposed next steps:
1) I share a proposed redline that maps uptime bands to credits.
2) Marcus and infra evaluate what's required for 99.99 (regional active-active, additional reserved capacity).
3) We scope a short pilot for Dedicated instances (30 days) if Acme wants to validate the higher SLO before committing.

I'll follow up internally and send a concrete proposal by early next week.

Best,

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: FW: SLA discussion — uptime & latency commitments

Forwarding Acme's request; procurement is pushing for 99.99% and automatic credits. Can you advise on the feasibility and the minimum requirements (tech + cost) to support 99.99 for a production workload? If 99.99 isn't realistic for hosted, what is the narrowest amendment we can offer for Dedicated?

Key asks from Acme: 99.99 uptime, automatic monthly credits, a p99 latency commitment. They want a clause in the SLA that doesn't require a claims process for credits.

Thanks — Laura

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-05T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: SLA discussion — uptime & latency commitments

Short answer: 99.99% is possible but only with Dedicated, multi-region active-active and explicit redundancy/traffic-splitting. Hosted multi-tenant plane is designed for 99.9% SLOs not 99.99 without significant overprovisioning. Considerations:

- Uptime math: 99.9% monthly downtime budget ≈ 43.8 minutes; 99.99% ≈ 4.38 minutes. Achieving the latter reliably requires region failover and cross-region KV cache coherence (more engineering and cost).

- Latency: p99 depends on tail behavior (large prompts, KV-cache cold starts). For Dedicated we can commit p99 at ~200ms for typical prompt sizes (≤1k tokens) with reservation & warmed caches; for hosted, p99 will be wider (up to ~500ms) unless customer invests in reserved slots.

- Credits mechanics: we can implement automatic credits when observability pipelines detect an SLO breach for a region and aggregate across the billing period; needs small instrumentation change and legal sign-off on the calculation method.

- Exclusions we recommend: scheduled maintenance (with 72h notice for major), customer misconfiguration, DDoS where mitigations are in progress, and third-party infra incidents (cloud provider).

Recommend a proposal:
1) Offer Acme Dedicated (reserved capacity) with a 99.95% uptime SLA by default; elevate to 99.99% for an added fee and a short architecture runbook (active-active across two regions).
2) Automatic monthly credits: sliding scale tied to monthly uptime percentage; calculation automated by our observability team.
3) Latency: p95/p99 targets included only for Dedicated.

If legal wants numeric credit bands I can draft them; Rishi — can you confirm commercial willingness to price the added redundancy?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2025-11-06T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed SLA terms for Acme — Dedicated option + credits (for review)

Hi Tom — thanks for the patience. After internal alignment, here is a concrete proposal we believe balances availability, tail-latency, and economics. Attached is a proposed redline for your procurement team. High level: 

1) Deployment mode: Dedicated (reserved capacity) recommended for production-sensitive workloads. If you must use Hosted, see the hosted fallback below.

2) Uptime commitments (monthly):
   - Dedicated standard: 99.95%
   - Dedicated (premium architecture, optional, + pricing adder): 99.99% (requires active-active across two regions and a short runbook)
   - Hosted API: 99.9% (no change)

3) Credits (automatic monthly application):
   - For Dedicated (applies to monthly invoice for the service in scope):
       * Uptime >= 99.95%: 0% credit
       * 99.95% > Uptime >= 99.5%: 10% credit
       * 99.5% > Uptime >= 99.0%: 25% credit
       * Uptime < 99.0%: 50% credit (rare, severe outages)
   - For Hosted API: existing schedule — up to 10% credit for sustained outages.

4) Latency commitments (for Dedicated):
   - p95 request latency: <= 250ms
   - p99 request latency: <= 200ms (for typical prompt sizes under 1k tokens; specific prompt distributions should be included in the runbook)

5) Exclusions & maintenance: Scheduled maintenance windows (we'll provide 7x24 notice for major changes, routine patching excluded if within agreed windows), customer-caused incidents, force majeure, and cloud provider outages beyond our control.

6) Ops & reporting: Automatic crediting (no customer claims required) based on our observability pipeline; we will provide a monthly SLO report and a dedicated incident postmortem within 5 business days for Sev 1 outages.

7) Next steps:
   - I attach the redline to the SLA (Redwood-SLA-draft-v3.pdf) with the Dedicated amendment inserted.
   - If Acme agrees, we'll generate the final SLA for signature (DocuSign link) and can schedule a 30-day Dedicated pilot to validate p99 latency.

Would you like the 99.99 premium architecture cost estimate included in the redline or as a separate amendment?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood-SLA-draft-v3.pdf (redline)
Related link: https://docs.redwood.com/sla/ACME-2025-11

From: Tom Keller <tom.keller@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Proposed SLA terms for Acme — Dedicated option + credits (for review)

Laura — thanks for the detailed proposal. This is broadly in line with what procurement needs. Two small asks before we finalize:

1) Credits automation: We prefer credits to be applied automatically to the customer's billing statement (no claims process). Your note says automatic — can you confirm the exact calculation will be visible to us in the monthly SLO report? We also need the formula in the SLA (how downtime is measured and rounded).

2) Weekly incident digest: for the first 90 days post-signature, could Redwood provide a weekly incident digest (summary of any incidents, mitigations, and ETA to resolution) in addition to the monthly report?

If you confirm both, procurement can greenlight and I'll route the DocuSign for signature.

—Tom

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2025-11-10T16:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA terms for Acme — Dedicated option + credits (for review)

Tom — great, and thanks for the clarity. Confirming:

1) Automatic credits: yes — credits will be applied automatically to the next invoice. The SLA redline now includes the exact calculation clause: monthly downtime is measured in seconds across the service boundary, rounded to the nearest second; uptime% = (total_seconds_in_month - downtime_seconds) / total_seconds_in_month * 100. Our monthly SLO report will include the raw metrics, the downtime windows (UTC timestamps), and the computed credit amount.

2) Weekly incident digest: agreed for the first 90 days post-signature. We'll send a short weekly email with any incidents, status, and mitigation notes.

I have updated the attached final SLA for signature. Once you sign, we'll prepare a PO and schedule the Dedicated pilot (if desired).
